subject: Renewal synchrony + top-up cadence proposal

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0500
Subject: Renewal synchrony + top-up cadence proposal

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation I sketched a proposal that aligns your renewal boundary with LunarHealth's fiscal year while giving you a predictable monthly top-up cadence for burst months. High level: 

- Convert current annual subscription (ends 2027-03-31) into a 24-month agreement that co-terms to FY-2028 (new term ends 2028-12-31).
- Maintain current committed baseline (50M tokens/month) and add a small monthly top-up bucket that auto-replenishes for three high-volume months per quarter.
- Keep an auto-renew option but allow a 60-day opt-out window for procurement.
- Include a one-time onboarding credit (applied to Q1 FY-2027 usage) to offset migration overhead.

I've attached a simple workbook that shows the proposed cadence and a draft SOW stub for your legal/ops team. Can you confirm whether co-terming to calendar-year fiscal boundaries is acceptable on your end? If yes, we'll scope the exact token bands and produce a redline-ready amendment.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm fiscal boundary preference (FY vs calendar).
2) Procurement provides any required billing/legal constraints (PO cadence, invoice net terms).
3) We send a pricing amendment + MMP (mutual action plan) and target signature in 3 weeks.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 20m call if helpful.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0182

Aditya —

Thanks for the write-up, this looks close to what we discussed. A few clarifying points from product/ops: 

- Co-terming to FY-2028 is preferred (we operate on a July–June fiscal year). If we co-term to FY-2028 would the effective start be 2027-07-01?
- We need the top-up mechanic to support per-project attribution — ideally each top-up instance can be mapped to a project ID so we can bill internally.
- For procurement: standard net-30 invoices, we prefer quarterly invoicing but can consider monthly billing if there's no material uplift in processing overhead.

I've attached our November usage export for reference; you can see the three big burst weeks tied to our telemedicine pilot.

Cc'ing procurement and Ben (who runs cost allocation) — procurement, please flag any legal/billing constraints.

Best,
Sarah

LunarHealth

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the file; that burst pattern is exactly what our top-up cadence is built for. A few practical notes from pricing and ops: 

- If your fiscal year is July–June we can set the new term to start 2027-07-01 and end 2029-06-30 (24 months) so you get alignment with internal budgets.
- Top-up design: we can create named top-up buckets tied to project IDs (e.g., TELEMED-PILOT) and produce a monthly usage export that includes project tags for your internal allocation.
- Billing cadence: quarterly invoicing with a monthly usage detail attachment works for us; we'll keep net-30.

Attached is a worksheet with two pricing variants: (A) lower per-token overage with a higher committed baseline, (B) smaller baseline + larger top-up per-quarter. Which would you prefer for the pilot projects?

I'll open a HubSpot task and draft the amendment once you confirm variant A vs B. HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

Thanks — happy to coordinate a short call next week to walk through the workbook.

Neha Kapoor

Hi Neha / Aditya —

Procurement reviewing. A few legal/billing items to call out before we can accept a co-term amendment: 

- We require purchase order numbers at the point of signature and prefer quarterly consolidated invoices tied to POs.
- DocuSign must present a single amendment PDF (no separate SOW attachments that need separate signatures).
- We need a clause that allows for an annual pricing review tied to CPI (consumer price index) with a cap (we typically accept up to 3% year-over-year).
- Auto-renew is acceptable only if we have an opt-out notice at least 60 days prior to renewal and a clear process for cancellation that does not incur penalties if usage falls below committed baseline.

Please prepare a single amendment PDF with the above incorporated. Also, can you confirm whether Redwood can support a quarterly pre-bill estimate (for our internal budget team) so we can allocate funds ahead of invoices?

Regards,
LunarHealth Procurement
procurement@lunarhealth.com

Thanks — this is very clear, appreciate the details. Quick confirmations from our side: 

- We'll produce a single amendment PDF that includes the SOW as an appendix and supports DocuSign single-envelope execution.
- PO number support: yes — we will include a PO field on the invoice and support quarterly consolidated invoices.
- Pricing review: we'll include a CPI-based annual review clause with a max 3% cap.
- Auto-renew: we'll include a 60-day opt-out process, and explicit language that no penalty applies if usage drops below the committed baseline (overage/true-up will apply as usual).
- Quarterly pre-bill: we can generate an estimated pre-bill at month-end (estimates only) broken down by project tags so your budget team can reserve funds.

Next steps for Redwood: Neha will prepare two redline variations (Variant A/B) with the amendment assembled into a single PDF and post the HubSpot deal update. We'll aim to get the first draft into your hands by EOD Thursday.

I'll also send the DocuSign envelope link once the amendment is ready.
